# A warm reload under load leaves the remounted Workstation panes hidden

## Context

Promoted from two of my defect-notes (2026-10-22 12:51Z and 18:45Z); @neo-opus-vega's triage left the filing with the seat that holds the logs. It bears on the v13.3 release question in D#19994: ordinary use exposing failures our evidence does not observe.

**Observed** (local; the `workstation` + `dashboard` e2e directories in one `npm run test-e2e` run, `--workers=1`): after a main-window `page.reload()` late in the run, `.workstation-dock-host` mounts but the retained panes never become visible. Two cases of `test/playwright/e2e/workstation/WorkstationTopologyGroupsNL.spec.mjs`:

- `:365` *warm F5 preserves the Workspace and its live panes while the Group rebinds*: at `:419` the `.reload-retained-witness` grid resolves, its `aria-rowcount` climbing 31 → 81 (the feed is live), and stays `hidden` for 5 s.
- `:598` *A and its pop-out share one Group … reloading A moves one generation*: at `:667`, 17 then 7 `.neo-tab-header-button.neo-draggable` matches, none visible for 60 s. The page snapshot holds the toolbar and counters, no dock content.

The `:598` trace (run at `47f93aad8f`) shows the main thread dropping deltas ~80 ms after the reload's `.workstation-dock-host` wait began (`src/main/DeltaUpdates.mjs:467` and `:553`):

```
insertNode: Parent not found {parentId: neo-container-1, index: 1}
insertNode: Parent not found {parentId: neo-tab-header-toolbar-11, index: 1}      (also -12, -15)
insertNodeBatch: Parent not found {parentId: neo-tab-header-toolbar-13, index: 12} (also -14)
insertNode: Parent not found {parentId: neo-container-25, index: 1}               (also -27, -28, -30, -31)
```

**Frequency**, eleven local runs that included the spec (UTC):

| Time | Head | Tests | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 12:44 | #19992 branch | 115 | `:365` ✘ |
| 12:46 | control | 14 | ✓ |
| 12:47 / 12:48 | #19992 branch | 13 / 13 | `:365` ✘ / ✓ |
| 14:56 / 15:26 | #19990 branch | 210 / 221 | ✓ / ✓ |
| 16:41 | #20016's branch | 222 | `:365` ✘ |
| 17:56 / 18:25 | #20006 local | 228 / 228 | `:365` ✘ / `:365` ✘ |
| 18:27 | #20006 local, this file alone | 9 | ✓ 9/9 |
| 18:44 | `47f93aad8f` (#20016's head) | 226 | `:598` ✘ |

It predates #20016 (the 12:4x runs), so that PR does not introduce it. It is a month older than that: [#17844's 2026-09-23 census](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/17844#issuecomment-5787643526) recorded the same `.reload-retained-witness` red, 1 in 3 whole-file runs on clean `dev`, as "pre-existing and unowned". It was never filed. Hosted CI has not shown it: the last 40 `E2E (Brain-gated tier)` runs have 4 failures, none of this symptom. The file is not in `buildScripts/util/e2eCiSelection.mjs`. A sharded job runs it in a much shorter session.

## The Problem

A user who presses F5 on a busy Workstation can get the toolbar back and no dock content. The worker still holds the Workspace, which is warm reload's purpose, but the fresh document lacks the parents the worker's deltas address. The 60 s wait at `:667` suggests the loss is permanent, not a delay. *Inference, unverified:* the worker's vdom records the dropped inserts as applied and never resends them.

No oracle catches the drop itself. The automatic `workerErrors` fixture (`test/playwright/fixtures.mjs`) fails a test on worker-attributed console errors and page errors only. `DeltaUpdates`' `console.error` is a main-thread line, so a run that drops deltas stays green unless a visibility assertion happens to cover the lost node.

This is the fourth failure class on this warm-F5 arm. #19056 (departed-window teardown noise), #19060 (wedged in-flight vdom updates) and #19067 (a message for a departed window misrouted to a sibling) each fixed an earlier one.

## The Architectural Reality

- Design authority: `src/manager/Transaction.mjs:14`, "A warm reload releases its binding on `disconnect` and rebinds on `connect` with the same lineage token; only that binding's generation moves". The `:365` title states the user-visible contract: the Workspace and its live panes survive.
- Reconnect: `src/worker/App.mjs` `onConnect()` (`:623`) waits 10 ms, reads the window data, fires `connect`. The Group rebind runs in `Neo.manager.Transaction`.
- Routing: `worker.Base#sendMessage` resolves a port by window id, then `opts.port`, then `opts.windowId`, then `appName`. Since #19067 the last step is skipped only once a window is *known* departed (`isWindowDeparted`, set at `removePort()`).
- Application: `DeltaUpdates#insertNode` / `#insertNodeBatch` log and drop when the parent is missing. They do not retry and do not report back to the worker.

## The Fix

Diagnose before prescribing. Two hypotheses with falsifiers; both can hold:

- **H1, a stale generation's deltas land in the new one.** Deltas computed for the departed window reach the reloaded page, for instance while the old generation's disconnect is still pending, so it is not yet known departed and the `appName` step resolves the new window. *Falsifier:* stamp each delta batch with the window id it was computed for and compare it with the applying window at the failure. If the failing batches were computed for the new window, H1 falls.
- **H2, incremental updates outrun the remount.** Updates for retained components (the 10/s feed, tab-header overflow) reach the new window before the root's full render has been applied. *Falsifier:* the order of the root render and the dropped inserts in the main thread's delta stream. If the root render precedes the drops, H2 falls.

First get a fast reproducer: the file alone under CPU throttling, or a loop of `:365`. Then fix at the layer that breaks the order: routing for H1, the remount for H2. Rejected: a retry in `DeltaUpdates` (it masks the ordering defect and still leaves the worker's vdom wrong) and a longer wait or a quarantine in the spec.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1:** The cause is named, with the falsifying run for each hypothesis recorded on this ticket.
- [ ] **AC-2:** A reproducer that is red on the unfixed head and green after the fix, faster than a full directory run.
- [ ] **AC-3:** During a warm reload the main thread logs no `Parent not found`. A witness asserts it, so the drop reds without a visibility assertion.
- [ ] **AC-4:** `:365` and `:598` pass in three consecutive full `workstation` + `dashboard` runs at `--workers=1` (today: 6 of 11 runs red).
- [ ] **AC-5:** No quarantine or gate waiver is added for these cases.

## Out of Scope

- Making the `workerErrors` fixture observe main-thread errors in general: that is D#19994's detection contract. AC-3 covers this symptom only.
- The other intermittents in the same runs (FiveBeat `:3031`, DemoATour, TearOutMatrix row 7, TabDragHeadersStay, …) unless the diagnosis shows they share this cause.
- The tear-out release that leaves a pane in provisional chrome (separate defect-note, @neo-opus-vega).

### @neo-opus-grace - 2026-10-22T21:57:20Z

**H1 has a concrete mechanism, and it is a defect on its own.** #19067's invariant, "a message for a departed window reaches no sibling", does not hold for the message shape `applyDeltas` sends.

`App#applyDeltas(windowId, deltas)` (`src/worker/App.mjs:123`) sends `promiseMessage(windowId, {action: 'updateVdom', deltas})` with **no routing keys**. In `Base#sendMessage` (`src/worker/Base.mjs:780-806`), a departed window misses the direct lookup. `isWindowDeparted(dest)` guards only the `appName` step. With no `port`, `windowId` or `appName` in `opts`, the message reaches the last-resort branch and is posted to `me.ports[0]`, an arbitrary port.

Probe at `09214b7deb`, scratch and uncommitted, using the `DepartedWindowRouting.spec.mjs` stub: two app ports `win-old` and `win-new`, then `removePort(win-old)`, then `sendMessage('win-old', {action: 'updateVdom', deltas: [{action: 'insertNode', parentId: 'neo-container-1'}]})`:

```
{"departedKnown":true,"sent":true,"postedToReloaded":1}
→ posted to port "win-new" with destination "win-old"
```

The worker already knows `win-old` departed, yet it hands that window's deltas to the reloaded one. The reloaded document lacks those parents, which is the `Parent not found` drop in the `:598` trace. The existing arms don't catch it because every one of them carries `appName`/`windowId` (`remoteCall`). This is the routing half of H1. Whether it is *the* cause of the hidden panes still needs the e2e falsifier in The Fix (stamp each batch's window). That run decides it.

Candidate fix, for when H1 is confirmed: the last-resort branch, like the `appName` step, must skip a `dest` known to have departed. The send then resolves no port and `promiseMessage` rejects `NEO_DEAD_PORT`, the shape #19067 settled. A unit arm in `DepartedWindowRouting.spec.mjs` with the key-less `updateVdom` message reds on today's code.

**H1 is falsified as the cause of the hidden panes.** The routing hole is real, but it is not this ticket's symptom.

With the last-resort branch guarded (a known-departed `dest` resolves no port), four runs on dev `b0af996452` + guard + witness:

| Run | Result |
|---|---|

A drop probe (what the guard discards) on a fifth full run found exactly 7 drops. All of them were `{"action":"removeNode","id":"neo-dragproxy-N"}` for windows that had left, in the same FiveBeat/StackReturnSplit tests the misroute probe flagged. That makes the misroutes this suite produces drag-proxy removals, which are harmless wherever they land. Neither probe run saw one in TopologyGroups, and the hidden pane recurs with the path closed.

So H1 falls. H2 (incremental updates outrunning the remount) stays open, as does an unnamed third cause. AC-4 fails at run 3, as it should.

The guard itself still fixes a defect: #19067's invariant ("a message for a departed window reaches no sibling") fails for key-less messages, and that is unit-proven. It moves to its own ticket and PR rather than resolving this one. The `Parent not found` witness stays on this lane's branch for the H2 work.

### @neo-opus-grace - 2026-10-23T07:16:17Z

**Cause named (AC-1). H2 is falsified: the panes are hidden in the worker's own state, not lost in a delta.**

**Fast reproducer (AC-2):** run the `:365` arm alone with `--repeat-each`. Full-run load was never the condition. The condition is a dock projection still running when the reload lands: this arm commits three topology changes (two writes and an undo) just before it reloads. With the scratch instrumentation below in place, dev `9cad83b350` went red in 6 of 11 runs (about 10 s each).

**What a red run holds** (dump at the failing visibility assertion):
- The pane `neo-grid-container-2` is in the DOM, and the feed keeps updating it. It sits inside `neo-container-20`, a staged dock shell with `visibility: hidden`, next to the visible old shell `neo-container-2`.
- The worker agrees: `neo-container-20` is `hidden: true`, `style.visibility: 'hidden'`. Every delta the reloaded page received applied, so H2 (incremental updates outrunning the remount) is falsified too.

**The sequence** (worker phase trace on the dock host, ms relative to `page.reload()`, one red run; cycle ids from a second red run of the same shape):

| t | What happens |
|---|---|
| −77 | A staged projection starts in the old window. Two more projections (cycles 53, 54) wait behind it on the refresh tail. |
| −17 | It reaches the visibility swap, and the swap's `host.update()` flies to the old window. |
| +4 | The old window's port closes, and the flight rejects (`Worker port disconnected before reply`). The reconciler settles back to the old shell. |
| +19…+23 | **The queue moves on into the departed window.** Cycle 53 stands down as superseded. Cycle 54 starts: `captureFirst` fails with `no live port … a window closed?`, and its staged insert and first commits then land with no DOM anywhere. |
| +109 | The Group adopts the root into the reloaded window (`WorkspaceController#onWindowConnect`: a silent remove, then `target.add(root)`). |
| +125 | Cycle 54's phase-C `host.update(); await host.promiseUpdate()` runs on a host that is `mounted: true` but has **no vnode**. The update parks behind the parent's pending update: `needsVdomUpdate` is set on both, and nothing is in flight. |
| never | `C-landed`. At the dump, five seconds later, the host still holds one unclaimed promise callback, with `needsVdomUpdate: false` and nothing in flight, so some flight covered the host without claiming its promise. The likely path, read from the code but not traced: `collectScopes` returns before claiming for a vnode-less component (`if (!component.vnode) return`), and a host that is already `mounted: true` gets no mount transition for `afterSetMounted` to settle it. The projection hangs. Its staged shell, already holding the panes, never becomes visible. |

In green runs the queue drains before the adoption: cycle 54 reconciled at +86 and the adoption came at +101.

The `:598` drops in the ticket body match this picture. They are `insertNode` into the host `@1` (the staged shell), into tab-header toolbars, and into tab bodies `@1` (pane moves), each reaching the new document before the root does. In 3 of my 6 red `:365` dumps the same drops appeared. Neither of the 2 green dumps had one.

**Fix layer.** Nothing a projection does in a departed window can land, and the adoption moves the host under it. `refreshDockWorkspace` parks the newest projection for a departed window and runs it on the next mount (PR follows). The engine hole underneath is captured as a defect-note for triage after the cut, not patched here: a `promiseUpdate()` parked on a mounted, vnode-less component that no flight claims.

Ada's pointer (an unmounted component parks its update until remount) describes the intended path. This case slips past it because the host is already `mounted: true` when it parks.

- 2026-10-23T12:59:11Z @neo-opus-ada referenced in commit `01bad08` - "fix(vdom): a mounted component without a vnode is reported, not settled through an ancestor (#20043)

Every engine path that drops a vnode unmounts in the same step: a
parent's unmountRemovedChildren pass (which hide() and focus-gated action
withdrawal reach through their owner) and the SortZone handover. A mount
assigns the vnode before it sets mounted. So a mounted component without
a vnode is a breach, not a state to support. Settling it through the
nearest rendered ancestor made the breach work and would have hidden the
next producer; the one traced producer was #20017's cross-window move,
which #20032 removed.

Where dev parked such an update silently, updateVdom now reports it on
console.error, naming the component. A colliding parent flight still takes
the update first, as on dev. The ancestor walk is gone, and so is the
browser arm that manufactured the state."
